body.estimand_functional: \(\widehat L=L(\widehat{\mathbf P})\); \(B_N^{\mathrm{mean}}=(\max\{0,\|\bar X\|_2-(\alpha N)^{-1/2}\})^2\in\mathcal H_\alpha\) is a fully specified mean-only rule, while \(B_N^{\mathrm{plug}}=\max\{0,\widehat L-U_{N,K}/\alpha\}\in\mathcal H_\alpha\) is theoretical because its finite constant \(C_d\) is established only existentially. The proved functionals satisfy \(c_d\max\{N^{-1/2},K^{-2}(m\log m)^{-2/d}\}\le R_d(N,K)\le C_d[N^{-1/2}+\min\{r/K^2,K^{-1}m^{-2/d}\}]\) and \(c_{d,\alpha}N^{-1/2}\le E_{d,\alpha}(N,K)\le C_{d,\alpha}[N^{-1/2}+\min\{r/K^2,K^{-1}m^{-2/d}\}]\); both are \(\asymp N^{-1/2}\) when \(K\ge c_0N^{q_d}\). Exact \(\rho_{\mathrm{est}}\) and \(\rho_{\mathrm{len}}\) remain targets only on legal arrays with \(\liminf_NK_N/N^{q_d}=0\).

sampling_model.design: Balanced \(K=K_N\)-arm product experiment with \(N=Km\) and fixed \(d>4\).
sampling_model.units: For arm \(k\), \(X_{k1},\ldots,X_{km}\) are identically distributed from the arbitrary marginal \(P_k\) on \(\mathbb B_d\); all arm samples are independent.
sampling_model.treatment: The observed experiment supplies one independent sample from each potential-outcome marginal and leaves the within-unit \(K\)-world coupling unidentified.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Each marginal is estimated empirically. No density, smoothness, joint-mixability, known nuisance, or centered-variance substitution is imposed.

body.tldr: The target \(L(\mathbf P)\) is the sharp causal second-moment endpoint compatible with the observed potential-outcome marginals, not the centered variance endpoint. On the common fixed-\(d>4\), \(K\ge3\), balanced arbitrary-margin class shared with Gao--Ge--Qian, the core proves the exact residual envelope \(\min\{K,d\}/K^2\), the sharp optimal-sum diameter, and a tighter theoretical plug-in risk bound. It follows that minimax estimation and uniformly honest one-sided expected excess length are both of order \(N^{-1/2}\) for \(K\gtrsim N^{q_d}\), where \(q_5=1/6\) and \(q_d=1/4\) for \(d\ge6\). The plug-in confidence rule is theoretical because the proof establishes the calibration constant \(C_d\) only existentially. Separately, \(B_N^{\mathrm{mean}}\) depends only on \((\bar X,N,\alpha)\), uses radius \((\alpha N)^{-1/2}\), and is a fully specified honest no-MOT baseline requiring neither \(\widehat L\) nor \(C_d\). The certified empirical-MOT procedure computes a primal--dual bracket for \(\widehat L\), but it does not numerically calibrate the theoretical plug-in rule. The exact fixed-\(K\) logarithms, intermediate transitions, and ordered one-sided converse remain open precisely for legal arrays with \(\liminf_NK_N/N^{q_d}=0\), including every zero-ratio subsequence. The finite-support family is only a search template: endpoint separation, mixture indistinguishability, and resistance to every rematching column remain to be certified.

project_justification.gap: On the common fixed-\(d>4\), \(K\ge3\), balanced arbitrary-margin class, Gao--Ge--Qian's Theorem 1 has high-dimensional term \(K^{-1/2}m^{-2/d}\), whereas the proved tightening has \(K^{-1}m^{-2/d}\) and the dimension-saturated cap \(r/K^2\). Their published scope is broader in \(d\) and includes \(K=2\), but the distributional class on the overlap is the same armwise product experiment over arbitrary \(\mathcal P(\mathbb B_d)^K\). The two-margin Manole--Niles-Weed lower construction is a subclass of this arbitrary-margin class, so its \(K^{-2}(m\log m)^{-2/d}\) converse transfers upward, but it leaves the arm and logarithmic gap unresolved. Uniform one-sided expected-length optimality is likewise proved only in the root-\(N\) region.
project_justification.niche: The squared-sum cost has shared fixed-dimensional geometry: all dual potentials obey one joint constraint, and arbitrary-subset exchanges constrain optimal sums. A sharp small-arm lower family must nevertheless remain separated under every alternative multi-arm rematching. This makes the missing result a coupled aggregate-complexity or simultaneous-rematching problem, rather than a repetition of two-margin transport.
project_justification.fill: The project proves the residual envelope, optimal-support diameter, improved theoretical plug-in upper bound, the \(q_d\) root-\(N\) estimation and honest-length region, and a fixed-dimensional rational primal--dual certificate for the empirical endpoint. It also retains a separate fully specified mean-floor rule using only \((\bar X,N,\alpha)\), with no MOT solve and no existential empirical-process constant. The finite-support simultaneous family is defined but not instantiated: its endpoint separation, mixture indistinguishability, strict off-contact slack, and resistance to every rematching column are explicit remaining targets. The residual exact-frontier question covers every legal array with lower-limit ratio zero, while positive-lower-bound subsequences use the proved root-\(N\) theorems.

body.related_work: Gao, Ge, and Qian define the same second-moment endpoint and prove a balanced-sample empirical upper bound. Their published class covers all dimensions and \(K\ge2\); this note's comparison is restricted to the common fixed-\(d>4\), \(K\ge3\), balanced overlap, where both models allow arbitrary unit-ball marginals and the balanced i.i.d. design induces the same armwise product law. Their Theorem 1 displays \(N^{-1/2}+\min\{K^{-1},K^{-1/2}m^{-2/d}\}\); the present theoretical upper theorem improves the cap to \(r/K^2\) and the active high-dimensional term to \(K^{-1}m^{-2/d}\). The independently retained mean-floor construction is not a claim about the sharp elbow: it is a fully specified no-MOT baseline. Manole and Niles-Weed supply a two-margin fuzzy-hypothesis lower order \((m\log m)^{-2/d}\); the declared two-margin embedding is a subclass construction, so its \(K^{-2}\)-scaled converse transfers upward to the arbitrary-margin class, but it does not match the multi-arm upper term. Binary covariate-aware transport results of Lin, Gao, Blanchet, and Glynn concern conditional or mirror relaxations under additional regularity and inform the framing without resolving this unconditional growing-arm frontier. Binary transform-entropy and Donsker results of Hundrieser and coauthors do not provide a contraction for a growing jointly conjugate tuple. Work on joint mixability by Wang and Wang and by Koike, Lin, and Wang treats selected scalar or identical-margin families rather than arbitrary heterogeneous vector marginals. Han and Zhu impose regular Monge structure; Weed and Bach study empirical-measure approximation; Kravtsova studies fixed finite supports. Manole, Balakrishnan, and Wasserman study sliced Wasserstein intervals, Ji, Lei, and Spector obtain validity from dual feasibility, and Armstrong and Kolesar motivate ordered one-sided criteria in a different Gaussian model. Cheryala, Alaya, and Bouzebda establish multi-margin dual attainment but not the aggregate statistical capacity needed here. Generic multimarginal computation results explain why the fixed-dimensional rational certificate is specialized. The conditional STAR audit uses the randomized experiment of Angrist, Lang, and Oreopoulos and does not extend Gao--Ge--Qian's balanced theorem to the native \(161/37/36\) cell sizes without the declared balanced subsampling.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The unresolved class is not merely globally \(K=o(N^{q_d})\): it consists of every legal array with \(\liminf_NK_N/N^{q_d}=0\). Any subsequence with a positive eventual lower bound is covered by the proved root-\(N\) theorems; an unsettled irregular subsequence contains a further subsequence on which the ratio tends to zero, and the final rate formula must remain valid through all such transitions. On these small-ratio subsequences, the available lower order \(K^{-2}(m\log m)^{-2/d}\) and upper contribution \(K^{-1}m^{-2/d}\) do not match. The finite-support perturbation template has not been instantiated with endpoint separation, product-mixture total variation at most \(1/4\), and nonnegative slack against every rematching column, while optimal-sum geometry alone does not yield a sharper aggregate jointly conjugate complexity theorem. The theoretical plug-in confidence bound additionally contains an existential \(C_d\), so the rational algorithm's computable bracket for \(\widehat L\) does not make that confidence rule numerically explicit. The separate mean-floor rule avoids both obstacles but yields only its valid no-MOT baseline guarantee. The computation theorem is fixed-dimensional and polynomial in \((K/\epsilon)^d\), not a generic polynomial-time exact-MOT result, and the STAR audit depends on a known finite scale and randomized balanced subsampling.
body.honest_scope: The maintained statistical class has fixed \(d>4\), \(K\ge3\), balanced independent arm samples with \(N=Km\), arbitrary marginals supported on \(\mathbb B_d\), and legal limits satisfying \(m\to\infty\). The estimand is the uncentered sharp second-moment endpoint \(L\). The exact residual envelope, optimal-sum diameter, improved plug-in upper bound, risk sandwich, \(q_d\) root-\(N\) estimation theorem, theoretical plug-in honest-length theorem, mean-only baseline corollaries, and rational empirical-MOT certificate are established. The fully specified mean rule \(B_N^{\mathrm{mean}}\) uses only \((\bar X,N,\alpha)\) and the radius \((\alpha N)^{-1/2}\); it neither evaluates \(\widehat L\), solves MOT, nor chooses \(C_d\), and its \(N^{1/4}\) many-arm corollary is retained as a computational baseline rather than advertised as the sharp elbow. The sharper \(B_N^{\mathrm{plug}}\) is uniformly honest in theory, but it is not numerically calibrated or directly reportable without a computable value of \(C_d\). Exact estimation and honest one-sided expected-length rates are claimed only as \(N^{-1/2}\) on arrays with \(K\ge c_0N^{q_d}\); for a legal array with \(\liminf_NK_N/N^{q_d}=0\), every positive-lower-bound subsequence is settled and every zero-ratio or arbitrarily-small-ratio subsequence remains within the open frontier. The finite family is not claimed to establish its required separation or rematching slack. The STAR audit remains conditional on its declared finite bound, affine scale, i.i.d. superpopulation law, complete randomization, and randomized balanced subsampling, and it does not validate the native unequal-cell calculation.
